solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Independent negotiator's first class, Edward's told

indicators.note: first says only the opening letter of the negotiator is used

parts.note: the first letter of negotiator; the 's joins it to what follows
a form is a school class
Ed is the usual short form of Edward; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: An independent negotiator, travelling first class, is being briefed by someone called Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone informed has been given the facts, which is to have been told about them.

clue.text: Do something under naughty child's influence

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
to act is to do something

explanation.surface: Misbehaving because a naughty child is a bad influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under the influence' is a stock phrase, but 'influence' alone is the definition; the apostrophe-s is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the effect one thing has on another.

clue.text: Left behind, fine bananas go rotten

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters of go rotten go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Fruit abandoned in a bowl ends up fine bananas that have gone rotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like the fruit going off, but it is the signal to rearrange GOROTTEN into ORGOTTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forgotten has been left out of mind, abandoned or left behind by memory.

clue.text: Area restricted by Iran, generally

indicators.note: restricted as in confined, so the answer is held within the following words

parts.note: iRAN GEnerally

explanation.surface: A zone that Iran broadly limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Generally' looks like an adverb for the whole sentence; it supplies the GE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a stretch of ground, as in a firing range or an animal's range.

clue.text: Impassioned article penned by Hemingway?

indicators.note: penned as in shut in a pen, so the article is enclosed by the writer's name

parts.note: Ernest Hemingway, the American novelist; these are the outer letters
a, the indefinite article; it goes after the first letter

explanation.surface: A passionate piece written by Hemingway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a piece of journalism, which Hemingway did write, but it is the word a; the question mark flags Hemingway as a first-name clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: intensely serious and sincere in feeling.

clue.text: Regularly trying to guard attention to detail

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so the letters are taken at a steady spacing: every second one

parts.note: tRyInGtOgUaRd: the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th, 10th and 12th letters

explanation.surface: Someone keeps trying to protect their meticulous habits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guard' looks like a container instruction, but it is just letters in the fodder; the even letters run across three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: thoroughness and strict precision are what close attention to detail amounts to.

clue.text: The same dialect in Barking

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: People speak the same local accent in Barking.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is a district of east London, so the surface reads as geography; barking also means mad, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: alike in every detail.

clue.text: Working with big cat, first gets scratched head

indicators.note: scratched as in struck out, so the first letter is deleted

parts.note: on, as in switched on and working
a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: A big cat at work gets its head scratched first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scratched head' reads as one phrase; split it after 'scratched'.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: the head, as in 'off your onion', meaning out of your mind; the round bulb suggests a skull.

clue.text: Indicates Romeo feels bad outside court

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: outside says the jumbled letters are wrapped round the court
bad means faulty, so the letters of feels come out wrong, in a new order

explanation.surface: Romeo, feeling wretched outside a courtroom, shows his distress plainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romeo' looks like Shakespeare's lover, but he is just a phonetic-alphabet letter; 'bad' scrambles the feelings, which wrap 'outside' the court.
explanation.definitionFit: To reflect something is to show or reveal it, so a result that reflects a trend indicates it.

clue.text: As printer's broken, I left colleagues

indicators.note: broken means smashed into pieces, so these letters are reassembled in a new order
left means departed, so the I is not among the letters reassembled

parts.note: printer, with the 's read as a link meaning is

explanation.surface: An office worker explains that the printer is broken, so they walked out on their coworkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' shuffles AS and PRINTER, and the I that 'left' is taken out; the eight letters remaining make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Partners are people who work alongside one another in a firm or venture, so they are colleagues.

clue.text: Reassurance from match official about position from which golf ball is played

indicators.note: about as in around, so the official's letters go round the golf position

parts.note: ref, short for referee; these are the outer letters

parts.words: position from which golf ball is played
parts.note: a golf ball's lie is where it rests to be hit; this goes in the middle

explanation.surface: A golfer takes comfort from a referee's ruling on where the ball may be played.
explanation.walkthrough: Golf has its own 'relief' (a free drop away from an obstruction), which suits the surface but is not the sense defined here.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the easing of worry that reassurance brings.

clue.text: Be very enthralled by story

indicators.note: enthralled once meant held in thrall, captive

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story; these are the outer letters
v = very, the standard abbreviation; it goes between the I and the E

explanation.surface: Someone is utterly captivated by a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be' is the definition in the sense of exist, not a verb joining the rest of the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of existing, as in 'to be or not to be'.

clue.text: Picked 100 stockings

parts.note: C = 100 in Roman numerals
hose is an old word for stockings

explanation.surface: Someone selected a hundred pairs of stockings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked' looks like an adjective describing the stockings, but it is the verb that defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are past tenses of selecting.

clue.text: Former lover awfully nice and set for life

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: awfully means very badly, so the letters of nice and set are badly scrambled into a new order
and gathers set together with nice, so both words go into the one pool of letters that is scrambled

explanation.surface: A former lover, terribly pleasant and comfortably provided for, is set up for life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' looks like an intensifier for 'nice', but with 'and' joining set to it, it rearranges NICESET into ISTENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Existence means being alive, the state of living, which is what life means.

clue.text: Exact time half of fabric is found in street

indicators.note: only half the word is wanted, so three of fabric's six letters are kept

parts.note: St = street; its two letters split to hold the other pieces

indicators.note: found in as in located inside, so the pieces sit within the street abbreviation

parts.note: t = time
the back half of fabRIC

explanation.surface: An instruction on exactly when a piece of cloth turns up on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not say which half of fabric; the back half is the one that fits the crossing letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: precise, as in a strict translation.

clue.text: Unorthodox type of soldier supporting current king

indicators.note: a support holds things up from below, so in a down answer the soldier sits under the other pieces

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
R = rex, Latin for king
a regular is a professional soldier in the standing army

explanation.surface: An unusual kind of soldier backs the reigning monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: An irregular is also a type of soldier, so the surface nearly hands over the whole answer while its wordplay supplies only the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: not following the usual rules or form.

clue.text: Delight European with new song

parts.note: E = European
n = new
a chant is a simple song

explanation.surface: Charm a continental listener with a fresh tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' only strings E and N to the song; it adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to charm, fittingly rooted in the idea of casting a spell by singing.

clue.text: Host may be oddly abandoned on a French trip

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are abandoned, left behind, so only the even ones stay

parts.note: mAyBe without its 1st, 3rd and 5th letters
un is French for a
to trip is to dance lightly, as in trip the light fantastic

explanation.surface: A party host might be left behind on a trip to France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' looks like a person throwing a party, but it is a host as in a great number.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in a less common sense: a host of things is a great plenty of them.

clue.text: Expression of delight after grown-up left fairground ride

indicators.note: after as in following, so the cry of delight comes behind grown-up

parts.note: big as in grown up
whee! is a cry of glee
L = left

explanation.surface: An adult shrieks with joy after getting off a fairground ride.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the usual British name for a Ferris wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the giant turning passenger wheel is one kind of fairground ride.

clue.text: Takes no notice of Italian gentleman moving spades to the rear

indicators.note: spades is S in card notation, and moving it to the rear shifts that letter from the front of the word to its end

parts.note: signore is Italian for sir or gentleman

explanation.surface: An Italian gentleman shifts his shovels to the back, ignoring someone.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'moving spades to the rear', spades looks like the garden tool, but in bridge notation it is S, which goes from the front of SIGNORE to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore someone is to pay them no attention, which is to take no notice of them.

clue.text: Prevent small tummy upset

parts.note: s = small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: to upset a pot is to knock it over, so in a down answer it is read upwards

parts.note: a pot is a pot belly

explanation.surface: Ward off a minor stomach upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' pairs naturally with 'tummy' as an illness; here it tells you to turn POT over.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to keep something from happening.

clue.text: Marine mammal was circling lone ray underwater, primarily

indicators.note: circling says the word was goes round the picked letters
primarily means first of all, so each of the three words before it gives its first letter

parts.note: the first letters of lone, ray and underwater

explanation.surface: A sea creature swims round a solitary ray beneath the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was' looks like a plain verb, but it is the container: 'primarily' takes initials and 'circling' puts the word was round them.
explanation.definitionFit: A walrus is a large tusked mammal of the Arctic seas, a sea-going mammal like a seal.

clue.text: More verbose with one in command

parts.note: w = with

indicators.note: in as in inside, so the one sits within command

parts.note: an order is a command; it holds the next piece
I = one in Roman numerals; it goes after the D

explanation.surface: Someone who takes charge becomes more long-winded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' reads as a joining word but supplies the W.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: using more words than needed.

clue.text: Pressing egg on part of the bible

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them
NT = New Testament

explanation.surface: Pushing someone forward with a passage of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg on' reads as one phrase meaning urge, but 'egg' alone gives URGE and 'on' places it above NT.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: needing immediate attention, as a pressing matter does.

clue.text: Criminal disturbed dog owner by river

indicators.note: by means beside, so the river is placed next to the rearranged letters
disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters of dog owner are put out of order

parts.note: R is the standard map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A troubled dog owner is spotted lurking near a river, perhaps up to no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' looks like it describes the dog owner's mood, but it reorders DOGOWNER into WRONGDOE, and 'by' sets R beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer is a person who breaks the law or does wrong, which makes them a criminal.

clue.text: Gets rid of topless competitions for knights

indicators.note: without a top, so in a down answer the first letter comes off

parts.note: jousts are mounted lance contests between knights

explanation.surface: Knights' tournaments are cleared of anything risqué.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' teases a racier picture, but it simply beheads the knightly contests.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to force out or expel.

clue.text: Tree, partly sheltered, leans over

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used
turned over, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: shelteRED LEans holds these letters

explanation.surface: A tree, half in shelter, bends over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leans over' reads as the tree tilting; 'over' is the reversal and 'leans' is letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a small tree with white flowers and dark berries.

clue.text: Unusually cross after eastern craft capsized

indicators.note: after as in following, so the cross comes behind eastern

parts.note: E = eastern
an X is a cross

indicators.note: a capsized boat is upside down, so in a down answer the craft is read upwards

parts.note: craft = art, skill

explanation.surface: Someone oddly angry after an oriental boat overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' and 'capsized' make a boat sinking; the craft is a skill. 'Cross' looks like angry but is the letter shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb use: extra careful means unusually careful.

clue.text: Gently moves frames uphill, finally — artists might require these

indicators.note: frames means surrounds, so the gently-moving word encloses the last letter

parts.note: to ease something is to move it gently

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the last letter of uphill is used

parts.note: the last letter of uphill

explanation.surface: Someone carefully carries picture frames up a slope, kit that painters will need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frames' looks like picture frames, a fit for artists, but it puts L ('uphill, finally') inside EASES.
explanation.definitionFit: Painters set their canvases on wooden stands while they work, and those stands are what artists require.

clue.text: Aloofness from cat I send out

indicators.note: out as in out of place, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

explanation.surface: A cat keeps its distance after being put outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send out' reads as a phrase about putting the cat out; 'out' alone is the anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of manner: emotional reserve, coolness towards others.

clue.text: Polish lieutenant protects us and Royal Engineers

indicators.note: to protect is to shield on every side, so the lieutenant's letters wrap round US

parts.note: Lt = lieutenant; these are the outer letters
taken as it stands; it goes between L and T
RE = Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A Polish officer guards our army engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is capitalised to look like the nationality; it is polish, a shine.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a gleaming shine or sheen on a surface.

clue.text: Most terrific girls revise at first before each exam

indicators.note: before says these letters come ahead of what follows
at first means at the beginning, so each of the two words before it gives its opening letter

parts.note: the first letters of girls and revise
a test is an exam

explanation.surface: Schoolgirls cram first thing ahead of every exam, which they think is the best plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Greatest means the best of all, superlative, so it matches the most terrific.
